description: TornadoNET is a 7-step end-to-end automation framework that helps community leaders and stakeholders achieve faster and more effective recovery assessment following a tornado. Tracking housing recovery using traditional methods, such as door-to-door surveys, is time-consuming and labor-intensive and delays critical post-disaster decision-making. To this end, street-view imagery, deep learning, and GIS can be used to facilitate recovery assessment. The framework and the recovery dataset in this project is invaluable to studying recovery across various disciplines as archived recovery dataset of past tornadoes are rare. The labeled dataset herein serves as a fundamental database for housing recovery data. As a result, future researchers can further expand this recovery database to other tornadoes or natural hazards. TornadoNET also allows the users to retrain the deep learning models on new datasets to improve the model performance or when the building architecture in a new community differs from the training dataset.
name: TornadoNET
